data.title: Smartwell Technology Corp. Outlines AI-Powered Agriculture Strategy and Dual AI Technology Platforms
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

August 21, 2026 – TheNewswire - VANCOUVER, BRITISH COLUMBIA – Smartwell Technology Corp. (the “Company” or “Smartwell”) (TSXV: SMWE) today outlined its technology platform and strategic priorities following its listing on the TSX Venture Exchange.

Smartwell is a Canadian agricultural technology company focused on applying artificial intelligence, agricultural data and intelligent automation to both indoor and outdoor agriculture. The Company has developed two distinct AI technology platforms for different agricultural environments: its Controlled Environment Agriculture (“CEA”) System, focused on AI-driven crop growth and production management for greenhouse and indoor agriculture operators, and its Yuntong Agricultural Remote Sensing and Data System, focused on AI-based satellite imagery and spectral recognition for outdoor agriculture. Yuntong is designed to serve large-scale farms as well as agricultural lenders and agricultural insurance companies.

Two AI Technology Platforms for Indoor and Outdoor Agriculture

Smartwell’s technology strategy is based on two distinct AI approaches designed for different agricultural environments and business requirements. The CEA platform is focused on the question of how crops should be grown and managed in controlled environments, using crop growth models, environmental data and automation technologies to support production decisions. The Yuntong platform is focused on identifying and monitoring crops and agricultural conditions across large outdoor areas, using satellite imagery, spectral information and AI analysis to convert remote sensing data into structured agricultural intelligence. Together, the two platforms address different but complementary areas of agricultural technology, spanning intelligent crop production and large-scale agricultural data analysis.

CEA: AI Crop Growth Intelligence for Greenhouse Operators

Smartwell’s CEA technology is primarily designed for greenhouse operators and other indoor agriculture businesses and is built around a dual-engine architecture combining plant growth mechanistic models with deep neural network data models. The mechanistic models incorporate principles from plant physiology, photobiology, water and nutrient dynamics, and crop disease and pest behavior to provide scientific constraints that reflect the underlying logic of plant growth. The deep neural network models analyze crop growth, environmental and image data using technologies including time-series prediction, deep learning and reinforcement learning to identify complex relationships that may not be captured by traditional rules or human experience alone. The two model layers interact and are continuously calibrated against one another, with the objective of combining scientific interpretability with data-driven precision. Smartwell’s CEA AI models have been trained and optimized using more than 250 million crop growth data and image samples. Model outputs can be connected to greenhouse automation systems to support irrigation, fertilization, ventilation, lighting and other production activities, helping greenhouse operators improve the precision, efficiency and automation of crop management.

Yuntong: AI Satellite Imagery and Spectral Recognition for Outdoor Agriculture

Unlike the CEA platform, which is designed for indoor agriculture, Smartwell’s Yuntong Agricultural Remote Sensing and Data System is focused on outdoor agriculture and large-scale agricultural operations, with target customers including large farms, agricultural lenders and agricultural insurance companies. Yuntong uses a separate AI technology architecture to analyze satellite remote sensing imagery, multispectral and hyperspectral data, incorporating small-sample learning and advanced AI techniques to reduce reliance on large volumes of manually labeled data. The technology is designed to support crop identification, agricultural field and acreage identification, crop condition and growth monitoring, and large-scale agricultural change detection. For large farms, Yuntong can provide broad-area crop and agricultural condition information; for agricultural lenders, the data can support assessment of agricultural assets, planting activities and production risks; and for agricultural insurers, the technology can support monitoring and analysis of agricultural conditions and potential production risks. By combining satellite imagery, spectral information and AI analysis, Yuntong is designed to convert large-scale outdoor agricultural data into commercially useful agricultural intelligence.

From Agricultural Data to Agricultural Intelligence

Although the CEA and Yuntong platforms use different AI technology approaches, they share a common strategic foundation: agricultural data, AI analysis and actionable agricultural intelligence. In indoor agriculture, Smartwell combines greenhouse sensor data, crop imagery and environmental information with AI crop growth models to generate production decisions and connect those decisions to automated systems. In outdoor agriculture, Smartwell uses satellite, spectral and other agricultural data to identify and analyze conditions across large geographic areas and convert remote sensing data into information that can support agricultural management, lending and insurance decisions. Together, these capabilities position Smartwell across two complementary areas of agricultural intelligence: intelligent indoor crop production and large-scale outdoor agricultural data intelligence.

Strategic Priorities Following TSXV Listing

Following its TSXV listing, Smartwell intends to continue advancing both AI technology platforms through commercialization and research and development. In indoor agriculture, the Company plans to expand the application of its CEA technology across greenhouse and other controlled-environment operations, develop additional crop and growth-stage models, and further improve model training, validation and automated execution. In outdoor agriculture, the Company plans to continue developing its small-sample AI, satellite imagery and spectral recognition technologies and expand their applications across large farms, agricultural lending and agricultural insurance. The Company also intends to continue developing its agricultural data capabilities and pursue customers and strategic opportunities in North America and other agricultural markets.

Building an AI Agriculture Technology Platform

Smartwell’s long-term strategy is to develop an AI agriculture technology platform spanning different agricultural production environments. In indoor agriculture, the Company helps greenhouse operators understand crop growth and optimize production decisions; in outdoor agriculture, the Company helps large farms, agricultural lenders and agricultural insurers understand crop and production conditions across large geographic areas. By applying different AI technologies—including crop growth AI, plant growth mechanistic modeling, deep neural networks, small-sample learning, satellite imagery and spectral analysis—to different agricultural challenges, Smartwell aims to develop technology solutions that can be deployed across crops, regions and agricultural applications.

About Smartwell Technology Corp.

Smartwell Technology Corp. (TSXV: SMWE) is a Canadian agricultural technology company focused on the application of artificial intelligence, agricultural data and intelligent automation in agriculture. The Company’s technology platform addresses two principal agricultural environments. Its Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA) System integrates AI crop growth models, IoT sensors and automation technologies to support greenhouse operators and other indoor agriculture businesses. Its Yuntong Agricultural Remote Sensing and Data System applies AI-based satellite imagery and spectral recognition technologies to outdoor agriculture and is designed to provide agricultural data and analysis to large farms, agricultural lenders and agricultural insurance companies. Smartwell is headquartered in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada.

For more information, please visit www.smartwell.info.

Forward-Looking Statements

This news release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of applicable Canadian securities legislation. Forward-looking statements include statements regarding Smartwell’s business strategy, technology development, commercialization plans, market expansion, future products and services, and the potential applications of the Company’s technologies.

Forward-looking statements are based on assumptions and estimates that are subject to various risks and uncertainties, including the Company’s ability to commercialize its technologies, develop and improve its AI models, expand its customer base, utilize agricultural data, execute its business strategy and obtain sufficient capital and resources.

Actual results and future events could differ materially from those anticipated in such statements due to known and unknown risks, uncertainties and other factors. Readers are cautioned not to place undue reliance on forward-looking statements. Smartwell undertakes no obligation to update forward-looking statements except as required by applicable securities laws.

data.title: Nvidia to put finishing touches on banner US earnings season
data.description:
Key points:
  • Main US indexes green; Dow out front, up ~0.8%
  • Materials lead S&P sector gainers; Utilities weakest group
  • Dollar ~flat; US crude up slightly; gold rises >2%; bitcoin rallies >6%
  • US 10-year Treasury yield rises to ~4.74%

NVIDIA TO PUT FINISHING TOUCHES ON BANNER U.S. EARNINGS SEASON

Nvidia reports next week after Wednesday's close, the last key release in a much-stronger-than-expected second-quarter U.S. earnings season.

Results are in as of Friday from 465 of the S&P 500 companies. Including companies that have reported along with estimates for the rest, year-over-year earnings growth for the quarter is now seen at 51.9%, the highest since 2021, according to LSEG data.

But Tajinder Dhillon, head of earnings and equity research at LSEG Data & Analytics, notes S&P 500 earnings growth is at 33.5% on an adjusted basis from a year ago, also the highest since 2021, when earnings rebounded from the start of the pandemic. That figure excludes mark-to-market gains from both Alphabet and Amazon.com , he says.

Still, some 85% of reports are beating analysts' earnings expectations versus 80% over the last four quarters, according to LSEG data.

Some of the strongest growth for the quarter has come from semiconductor companies, and investors remain focused on AI-related investments.

In its latest announcement, Nvidia on Friday said it has made a minority investment in privately held Cloverleaf Infrastructure to develop infrastructure to power AI data center projects across the U.S.

"AMD's a close No. 2 as far as the AI trade within semiconductors, and their earnings were strong, very, very strong," said Jake Dollarhide, chief executive officer of Longbow Asset Management in Tulsa, Oklahoma.

"Nvidia may be hard-pressed to impress investors," he said. "I don't think this is the quarter where they disappoint... (but) one of these times Nvidia is going to disappoint."

Peter Cardillo, chief market economist at Spartan Capital Securities in New York, notes that Nvidia is "a bit of a bellwether." He adds that "earnings season went extremely well, and if (Nvidia does) come out and beat, that could only be a plus."

data.title: Why a defense lawyer went on the offensive in an Oregon robocall lawsuit
data.description:
By Sara Randazzo

Most defense lawyers consider it a success if their adversary agrees to drop a lawsuit and move on.

But when a plaintiff tried to withdraw a consumer lawsuit against attorney Ryan Watstein's insurance client, he urged an Oregon federal judge to keep the case alive.

Watstein in court filings had laid out in dramatic detail why he believes serial plaintiffs and their lawyers have abused the class action system to make millions of dollars off a 1991 federal law meant to stop spam phone calls. He argued that the other side only wanted out of the case to avoid further scrutiny.

Before letting plaintiff Chet Wilson dismiss the case, Watstein told the judge this week, he should be able to probe for documents and depose witnesses to try to unravel the scheme. He alleges Wilson deliberately purchased a phone number to lure spam calls, and that a web of attorneys is pressing extortionate settlement demands under contingency arrangements that promise them 90% of any recoveries in a wave of similar cases.

Wilson's lawyers deny any wrongdoing and insist they and their client are just trying to stop illegal robocalls.

It all came to a head Wednesday at a hearing in front of Chief U.S. District Judge Michael McShane in Oregon, who expressed deep skepticism about the sincerity of Wilson’s intentions. The judge wondered aloud whether any criminal fraud was taking place and why no other defense lawyer had ever publicly pushed back rather than reaching quick settlements.

“Mr. Wilson and the lawyers who represent him are making a cottage industry out of this,” McShane said, before chiding Wilson’s attorney for making it sound like his client didn’t want to receive the spam calls. “Please don’t take me for an idiot up here.”

DIALING FOR DOLLARS

Watstein's campaign targets litigation stemming from the Telephone Consumer Protection Act, or TCPA, enacted by Congress to protect consumers against unwanted robocalls and junk faxes. It's expanded to include modern-day annoyances like spam text messages. Under the law, aggrieved consumers can sue the source of spam calls and collect between $500 and $1,500 per violation.

Wilson, an Oregon resident who acquired a number ending 999-9999, has filed more than 80 such TCPA lawsuits in recent years, all as proposed class actions. While some defendants have settled, he met resistance when suing Watstein's client, Freeway Insurance Services of America.

Wilson accused the insurer of texting him advertisements despite being on the national do-not-call registry. But in court filings, Watstein detailed how he believes a network of law firms around the country work with serial plaintiffs to gin up TCPA cases, including by using VPNs to enter numbers into online forms that lead to the spam calls.

At the heart of his allegations is a small D.C. legal shop called the Heidarpour Law Firm, which serves as a lead generator and then passes off clients to law firms that file the TCPA class actions. The Heidarpour firm has attracted some prior scrutiny from TCPA defendants, and Watstein was able to leverage information from hundreds of other cases defended by his firm and others to make his arguments.

Contracts involving Heidarpour that have emerged in court filings show that when the firm and its partner law firms settle a case, their clients are limited to recovering what a court could award under the TCPA's statutory cap, while the lawyers split the rest, which is often multiples more than that.

Clients also agree to give the firm power of attorney to settle and pursue claims on their behalf and to reimburse Heidarpour for expenses if they ever want to fire them, the documents show, which Watstein argues makes it difficult for anyone unhappy with the arrangement to walk away.

"This scheme results in millions of dollars in individual settlements," Watstein, the co-founder of Georgia litigation boutique Watstein Terepka, said at Wednesday's hearing. While the full scope of Wilson's settlements isn't clear, Watstein mentioned another serial TCPA plaintiff who settled 18 cases for $633,500, with almost 90% going to attorneys.

The Heidarpour firm didn't respond to a request for comment.

UNDER SCRUTINY

The number of TCPA lawsuits has been on the rise in recent years. There were 1,532 TCPA lawsuits filed in the first half of the year, according to litigation analytics firm WebRecon, up 34% from last year. Serial plaintiffs drove more than half of all TCPA litigation last year, according to risk management consulting firm CompliancePoint, filing an average of 3.6 cases each.

Heidarpour, whose website lists just one lawyer, isn't Wilson's counsel of record in the Oregon case. But when Watstein filed a subpoena against the firm in D.C. federal court, suspecting its involvement, the firm hired a high-powered team from Milbank to defend against it.

In a filing, Milbank partner and former acting U.S. solicitor general Neal Katyal argues the accusations against the Heidarpour firm are meritless. The firm doesn’t “manufacture” spam calls or texts on behalf of its clients, Katyal says, and despite the “power of attorney” provision, the firm doesn’t resolve claims without proper client sign-off.

The firm called Watstein’s claims “hyperbolic allegations” that don’t justify “the broad ranging fishing expedition” found in the subpoena. Katyal did not respond to requests for comment.

Beyond his focus on Heidarpour, Watstein also argued that the plaintiff in the Oregon case, Wilson, isn’t fit to serve as a class representative in this or any case. At the hearing and in court filings, he pointed to antisemitic and racist comments Wilson has repeatedly made online. Andrew Perrong, an attorney for Wilson, said in court he couldn’t defend the comments but that they shouldn’t make him ineligible to be a class representative.

In court, Perrong said Wilson had the unique phone number long before he started filing lawsuits, and that, "We bring every case intending to pursue class certification.” Perrong, based in Pennsylvania, was himself a serial TCPA plaintiff before he went to law school. Perrong didn't respond to a request for comment.

In the end, Watstein’s gambit paid off. Speaking from the bench, McShane said he would issue a ruling denying class certification, finding Wilson unfit to serve as a fiduciary in a class action. He also refused to dismiss the case until the defense gathers more information from Wilson and Heidarpour about their relationship.

The decision will impact a dozen or so other TCPA lawsuits filed by Wilson in Oregon federal court, including some that have recently settled.

McShane concluded that robust discovery is needed “to determine exactly what is going on.”

data.title: Walmart Opens 100th EV Fast-charging Site In US
data.description:
BENTONVILLE (dpa-AFX) - Walmart Inc. (WMT), an American multinational omnichannel retail corporation, said on Friday that it has opened its 100th company-owned and operated electric vehicle fast-charging site, expanding a network aimed at giving customers dependable charging while they shop.

The milestone site is located at the Walmart Supercenter on Jackson Creek Parkway in Monument, Colorado.

'By expanding EV fast charging at Walmart locations across the country, we're giving drivers a dependable way to charge while they're in the store,' said Shayne Wahlmeier, Senior Vice President, Walmart Energy.

Customers can start and pay for charging sessions through the Walmart app, with Walmart+ members receiving discounted rates. Open locations are also listed on major mapping platforms including Apple Maps, Google Maps, PlugShare, Chargehub and Chargeway.

Walmart said it will continue expanding its network in markets where customers need greater access to convenient fast charging, working with local utilities and partners to bring new sites online.

On the Nasdaq, shares of Walmart are currently losing 0.77 percent, changing hands at $102.79.

data.title: Trump administration moves to end attorney group's law school oversight
data.description:
Key points:
  • Education Department says ABA's law school arm lacks required independence from parent organization
  • ABA has clashed with the Trump administration over actions against judges and law firms
  • Accreditation advisory committee will consider the matter in September

By Karen Sloan

The U.S. Department of Education on Friday moved to strip the American Bar Association of its longstanding status as the federally recognized accreditor of U.S. law schools, deepening a clash between President Donald Trump's administration and the nation’s most high-profile lawyer organization.

Removing the ABA as the official overseer of law schools, a role it has filled since 1952, represents the administration’s latest effort to curtail the influence of the group, which a White House spokesperson in 2025 dismissed as a “snooty” organization of “leftist lawyers.”

In a lengthy report released on Friday, Education Department staff concluded that the ABA's Council of the Section of Legal Education and Admissions to the Bar is not "separate and independent" from the larger ABA as required. The report also faulted the ABA for being too slow to revise its rule requiring law schools to meet diversity standards.

A review of the ABA’s accreditation rules found it “out of compliance with the agency’s accreditation regulations and recognition standards,” an Education Department spokesperson said on Friday.

Revoking the ABA's accreditor status would disrupt federal student loan access for some law schools and could make it harder for law students to take the bar exam and become licensed attorneys in different states.

A bipartisan accreditation advisory committee will consider Friday's recommendation in September, with a final decision several months away.

The ABA's accreditation council will “address any misconceptions and clarify the record” when it meets with the federal advisory committee next month, its chairperson, Melissa Hart, said in a statement. She said the council is “confident” it can address the Education Department’s concerns.

DEEPENING CLASH WITH ABA

Trump signed an executive order in April 2025 directing Education Secretary Linda McMahon to assess whether to suspend or terminate the ABA as the government’s official law school accreditor, citing its “unlawful ‘diversity, equity, and inclusion’ requirements."

Since then, the ABA has sued the administration over canceled domestic violence grant funding and to challenge Trump's executive orders targeting individual law firms. The U.S. Department of Justice has barred its attorneys from speaking at or attending ABA events and curtailed the ABA’s longtime role in vetting judicial nominees.

The administration's move to end the organization's accreditor status comes despite recent efforts by the ABA’s law school wing to assert its independence from its parent organization and eliminate its DEI rule for law schools.

The ABA's policymaking body earlier this month voted against removing the DEI rule, but the legal education council was expected to push ahead with stripping the rule at a previously scheduled meeting on Friday.

data.title: US energy firms cut rigs for first time in four weeks, says Baker Hughes
data.description:
By Noel John

U.S. energy firms this week cut the number of rigs operating for the first time in four weeks, energy services firm Baker Hughes said in its closely followed report on Friday.

The total oil and gas rig count, an early indicator of future output, fell by five to 588 in the week to August 21. (BHGUSWTT), (BHGUSOILDRLW), (BHGUSGASDRLW) (USGSRC=ECI), (USOIRC=ECI)

Baker Hughes said the total count was still up 50 rigs, or 9.3%, from this time last year.

Baker Hughes said oil rigs fell by three to 452 this week, while gas rigs fell by one to 127 and other miscellaneous rigs fell by one to nine.

In the Permian, the nation's biggest oil-producing shale basin in West Texas and eastern New Mexico, the rig count rose by two to 267, the most since June 2025.

In the Eagle Ford shale in South Texas, the rig count rose by one to 50, the highest since June 2024.

In Texas, the state with the most rigs, the rig count rose by four to 281, the most since February 2025.

The oil and gas rig count declined by 7% in 2025, 5% in 2024, and 20% in 2023 as lower U.S. oil prices prompted energy firms to focus more on boosting shareholder returns and paying down debt rather than increasing output.

But spot U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude prices are expected to rise in 2026 due to supply disruptions in the Middle East from the Iran war after declining in 2023, 2024, and 2025.

data.title: Symbiotec Pharmalab IPO: Price band, lot size, GMP, listing date and other key details
data.description:
New Delhi, Aug. 21 -- The initial public offering (IPO) of Symbiotec Pharmalab is set to open on Monday, August 24. This will mark the 16th mainboard issue to hit Dalal Street this month.

Twelve issues have already debuted on the exchanges, with all of them currently trading above their respective issue prices. Along with Symbiotec Pharmalab, two other issues are scheduled to open for bidding on Monday, while another two will open towards the end of the month.

1. Symbiotec Pharmalab IPO date: The issue will open for subscription on Monday, August 24, and will remain open until Wednesday, August 27.

2. Symbiotec Pharmalab IPO price: The price band for the IPO has been fixed at Rs.938- Rs.988 per equity share.

3. Symbiotec Pharmalab IPO size: The company aims to raise Rs.1,757 crore through the IPO, which comprises a fresh issue of 0.15 crore shares aggregating to Rs.150 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 1.63 crore shares aggregating to Rs.1,607 crore.

As part of the OFS, promoter Satwani Holdings LLP and investors Rosewood Investments and India Business Excellence Fund-III will offload shares. The proceeds from the fresh issue will be used for debt repayment and general corporate purposes.

4. Symbiotec Pharmalab IPO lot size: The IPO lot size has been fixed at 15 shares, requiring a minimum investment of Rs.14,820 for retail investors.

5. Symbiotec Pharmalab IPO reservation: The IPO has reserved up to 50% of the net offer for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), at least 15% for non-institutional investors (NIIs), and at least 35% for retail investors.

6. Symbiotec Pharmalab IPO allotment date: The IPO allotment is expected to be finalised on Friday, August 28. Investors who receive an allotment will see the shares credited to their demat accounts by Monday, August 31, while refunds for unsuccessful bidders will also be initiated on the same day.

7. Symbiotec Pharmalab IPO listing: The mainboard IPO is proposed to list on both the NSE and BSE on Tuesday, September 1.

8. Symbiotec Pharmalab IPO GMP: According to market sources, the grey market premium (GMP) of the Symbiotec Pharmalab IPO stood at Rs.320 on Friday, indicating that the stock could list at a premium of around 32.40% over the upper end of the issue price band of Rs.988.

9. Symbiotec Pharmalab IPO book-running lead manager and registrar: JM Financial, Avendus Capital, Motilal Oswal, and Nomura Financial are the book-running lead managers to the issue, while MUFG Intime India Pvt. Ltd. is the registrar.

10. Symbiotec Pharmalab overview: Incorporated in 2002, Indore-based Symbiotec Pharmalab is a pharmaceutical and biotechnology company engaged in the development and manufacturing of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), nutritional ingredients, and specialty products.

The company serves domestic and international markets across regulated and emerging regions.

data.title: Harry Potter, Hello Kitty merchandise now in minutes: MINISO now on Swiggy Instamart
data.description:
New Delhi, Aug. 21 -- The quick commerce battleground is rapidly moving beyond last-minute groceries and household staples. In a move to capture the lucrative impulse-buying and gifting market, Swiggy Instamart announced a strategic partnership with global lifestyle retailer MINISO on Friday.

Consumers in key metropolitan cities can now order over 90 MINISO products, ranging from quirky stationery to officially licensed pop-culture merchandise, and have them delivered in just 10 minutes.

The collaboration marks MINISO's first foray into the quick commerce space in India. The initial catalogue rollout heavily targets Gen Z and millennial shoppers by focusing on MINISO's highly popular, IP-led merchandise.

Fans of globally recognised franchises can now instantly purchase products featuring characters from Harry Potter, Hello Kitty, My Melody, Kuromi, BT21, and Disney's Stitch.

The assortment spans multiple categories, including:

By placing these highly visual, emotionally driven products on a platform designed for instant gratification, Instamart is effectively turning its dark stores into digital mall storefronts, minus the wait typically associated with lifestyle and accessory shopping.

For Instamart, the integration of MINISO is a calculated step in its broader expansion into non-grocery categories, joining electronics, beauty, and toys.

"At Instamart, we're constantly bettering our assortment to reflect how and what customers shop today," said Gautam Swaroop, Chief Business Officer at Instamart.

"MINISO has created a unique space in the lifestyle category with products that are fun, functional, design-led, and accessible. By bringing the brand to Instamart, we're giving customers the convenience of getting these favourites delivered to their doorsteps while continuing to build a more comprehensive everyday shopping destination," Swaroop added.

The partnership also highlights a shifting distribution playbook for global physical retailers.

Facilitated by Opptra, MINISO's digital commerce distribution partner in India, the launch enabled the retailer to leverage quick-commerce logistics for rapid market penetration without relying solely on traditional mall footfall.

Charmaine Chan, Vice General Manager of MINISO India, emphasised the emotional connection of the brand's catalogue.

"From well-designed, high-quality, and value-for-money lifestyle products to IP collaborations and collectable toys that bring joy, comfort, and emotional connection, MINISO continues to make everyday life more fun and inspiring," Chan said. "Through our partnership with Opptra, we look forward to bringing MINISO closer to more consumers across India with greater speed and convenience."

While currently available in key metros, Instamart and MINISO plan to aggressively expand their product catalogues and city availability over the coming months. data.title: FTC Challenges Amgen's Patent Play in Enbrel Antitrust Case
data.description:
By Dean Seal

The Federal Trade Commission told a federal judge that Amgen's acquisition of rights to patent applications related to its arthritis drug Enbrel is subject to antitrust scrutiny.

The agency has filed a friend-of-the-court brief in private antitrust litigation that claims Amgen illegally acquired the rights to patent applications that it then shaped to cover Enbrel and eliminate low-cost competitors.

A federal judge already denied Amgen's motion to dismiss the case, which Amgen has since appealed on the grounds that its acquisition of patent applications, as opposed to issued patents, were immune from antitrust liability.

The FTC's filing doesn't technically support Amgen or CareFirst of Maryland, the lawsuit's plaintiff. But it does state that Amgen's arguments on appeal cut against the longstanding framework that acquiring a patent can violate antitrust laws if it boosts the purchaser's market power.

Patent applications can provide unique strategic advantages that can lead to more anticompetitive harm than acquiring an issued patent, the agency argued.

"Amgen's novel and sweeping arguments find no support in case law and, if accepted, would pose a substantial threat to competition," the FTC said.

The agency said it filed the brief because of its focus on making prescription drugs more affordable by promotion competition.

data.title: ITU-T Standardizes Framework of Low-Latency and Energy-Efficient Networks to Support the AI Era
data.description:
TOKYO, Aug 21, 2026 - (JCN Newswire) - KDDI Corporation, NTT, Inc., 1Finity Inc., a Fujitsu company and leading provider of global network solutions, NEC Corporation, Rakuten Mobile, Inc., Oki Electric Industry Co., Ltd., and Sumitomo Electric Industries, Ltd. today announced that the framework of low-latency and energy-efficient networks to support the AI era has been approved as an international standard by the International Telecommunication Union Telecommunication Standardization Sector (ITU-T) on August 13, 2026 [1].

This framework will contribute to the realization of All-Photonics Network (APN), a strategic field under the "Strategy for Realizing Next-Generation Information and Communication Infrastructure to Support AI Society - Beyond 5G Promotion Strategy 2.0 -" promoted by Japan?s Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications.

APN is expected to be deployed globally as a foundational network technology for next-generation services, including physical AI, because it enables high-capacity, low-latency, and energy-efficient communications and supports real-time processing of data obtained from sensors and robots in remote locations.

Toward this goal, the IOWN Global Forum, an organization dedicated to driving the widespread adoption of APN-based next-generation communication infrastructure, is developing common technical documents on APN architecture and functional requirements. In parallel, research and development on photonic network federation technology, which enables stable interconnection among APNs operated by different providers [2], is also underway to develop interconnection methods and evaluate them using actual equipment. However, achieving global-scale interoperability and adoption, including among operators, countries or regions outside these initiatives, requires establishing a common framework based on broad international consensus.

To address this challenge, Japanese telecommunications operators and equipment manufacturers have collaborated to lead the development of this framework. Now standardized as Recommendation ITU-T Y.3335, the framework defines the network configurations and technical requirements for establishing low-latency, energy-efficient communication paths across different operators [3]. It systematically organizes the accumulated knowledge of APNs and research outcomes on photonic network federation technology in a manner independent of any specific organization or implementation method. The approval from ITU-T provides a common framework for APN to be shared globally, making it easier to build APN services spanning multiple operators and enabling the use of high-speed, energy-efficient communication services even across geographically distributed sites.

The seven companies will continue to promote standardization activities in Japan and overseas by leveraging network technologies and standardization expertise cultivated in Japan. Within ITU-T, they are also contributing to the development of a Recommendation on functional architecture for low-latency and energy-efficient networks, targeted for October 2028, and will continue contributing to the global adoption of APN to support the AI era.

[1] KDDI Corporation, NTT, Inc., 1Finity Inc., NEC Corporation, and Rakuten Mobile, Inc. conducted this work as part of the commissioned research "Research and Development of All-Photonics Network Common Infrastructure Technology" (JPJ012368C09001) under the "Innovative ICT Fund Projects for Beyond 5G/6G" by National Institute of Information and Communications Technology (NICT), Japan.

[2] News release dated October 25, 2024Joint proposal by NTT, KDDI, Fujitsu, NEC, and Rakuten Mobile adopted as Japan's Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications/NICT's "Innovative ICT Fund Projects for Beyond 5G/6G" for social implementation and overseas expansion oriented strategic program (common infrastructure technology establishment)

[3] https://www.itu.int/rec/T-REC-Y.3335/en

About NEC

The NEC Group leverages technology to create social value and promote a more sustainable world where everyone has the chance to reach their full potential. NEC Corporation was established in 1899. Today, the NEC Group's approximately 110,000 employees utilize world-leading AI, security, and communications technologies to solve the most pressing needs of customers and society. For more information, please visit https://www.nec.com, and follow us on LinkedIn and YouTube.

data.title: Krait Critical Minerals Announces Receipt of Final Approval for CSE Listing and Commencement of Trading
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - August 21, 2026) - Krait Critical Minerals Corp. (CSE: KRIT) (the "Company" or "Krait") is pleased to announce that the Company has received final approval from the Canadian Securities Exchange ("CSE") to list its common shares (the "Common Shares") on the CSE (the "Listing").

Trading of the Common Shares is expected to commence at market open on Monday, August 24, 2026, under the symbol "KRIT". The Company has filed a final long-form prospectus dated August 13, 2026, with the applicable securities' regulatory authorities. The prospectus is available under the Company's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca.

"Receiving final approval to list on the CSE is a significant milestone for Krait and reflects the dedication of our team and supporters," said Oscar Mendoza, Chief Executive Officer of Krait. "The commencement of trading under the symbol KRIT will provide Krait with greater visibility, access to the public capital markets and a strong platform from which to grow the Company. We look forward to introducing Krait to the investment community and building long-term value for our shareholders."

About Krait Critical Minerals Corp.

Krait Critical Minerals Corp. is a Canadian junior mineral exploration company focused on acquiring and advancing prospective mineral properties in established North American mining jurisdictions. The Company's strategy is to combine disciplined project evaluation, modern exploration technologies and responsible field programs to identify and advance high-quality exploration opportunities with the potential to create long-term shareholder value.

Krait's flagship asset is the Goldbar Spider Lake Project in Ontario's Thunder Bay Mining Division, approximately 20 kilometres east of Terrace Bay and 30 kilometres west-northwest of Marathon. The 3,636-hectare (approximately 8,985-acre) property comprises 148 mining claims and 171 claim units, and Krait has an option to earn a 100% interest, subject to a 3% net smelter return royalty. Located within the western Schreiber-Hemlo Greenstone Belt, the project benefits from year-round access via Highway 17, nearby rail and power infrastructure, and proximity to established mining communities and service providers.

Investors are encouraged to visit Krait's new corporate website at www.kraitminerals.com to learn more about the Company, its Goldbar Spider Lake Project, management team, corporate strategy and latest news.

All Stakeholders are encouraged to follow the Company on LinkedIn , X.com, Facebook.
